'''Boris Yakovlevich Zeldovich''' ({{langx|ru|Бори́с Я́ковлевич Зельдо́вич}}; 23 April 1944 – 16 December 2018) was a Russian-American physicist and a son of the famous Soviet physicist [[Yakov Borisovich Zeldovich]]. He was doctor of the Physical and Mathematical sciences (from 1981) and a corresponding member of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ras.ru/win/db/show_per.asp?P=.id-359.ln-ru|publisher=Russian Academy of Sciences|title=Zeldovich, Boris Yakovlevich|accessdate=27 December 2018}}</ref> Since 1994 Zeldovich worked as a professor at the [[University of Central Florida College of Optics and Photonics|College of Optics and Photonics]] at the [[University of Central Florida]].<ref name=USU1/> During his lifetime he received a number of prestigious awards, including the [[USSR State Prize]] in 1983 and the [[Max Born Award]] in Physical Optics from the [[Optical Society]] (OSA) in 1997<ref name=USU1>{{cite web|url=https://www.creol.ucf.edu/person/boris-y-zeldovich/|title=Dr. Boris Y. Zeldovich|publisher=CREOL, The College of Optics & Photonics|accessdate=26 June 2019}}</ref><ref name=EncycChel>{{cite book|chapter-url=http://www.book-chel.ru/ind.php?id=5889&what=card|chapter=Zeldovich Boris Yakovlevich|publisher=Chelyabinsk: Kamennyi Poyas|accessdate=27 December 2018|language=Russian|year=2001|isbn=5-88771-026-8|title=Chelyabinsk. Entsiklopediya|editor=V. S. Boge |editor2=V. A. Chernozemtsev}}</ref> for his contributions to the fields of [[non-linear optics]], [[optical waveguide]] theory and optical holography. B.Zeldovich predicted and discovered, experimentally, the giant optical nonlinearity of liquid crystals, which is 10<sup>10</sup> times stronger than for usual media and is the co-discoverer of optical phase conjugation.<ref name="USU1" /><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Zel’dovich |first1=Boris Ya. |last2=Pilipetsky |first2=Nikolai F. |last3=Shkunov |first3=Vladimir V. |date=1985 |title=Principles of Phase Conjugation |url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-540-38959-0 |journal=Springer Series in Optical Sciences |volume=42 |language=en |doi=10.1007/978-3-540-38959-0 |bibcode=1985SSOS...42959.0Z |isbn=978-3-662-13573-0 |issn=0342-4111|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Zel’dovich |first1=Boris Ya |last2=Tabiryan |first2=N. V. |date=1985-12-01 |title=Orientational optical nonlinearity of liquid crystals |url=https://ufn.ru/en/articles/1985/12/a/ |journal=Physics-Uspekhi |language=en |volume=28 |issue=12 |pages=1059–1083 |issn=1063-7869}}</ref> He died on 16 December 2018 at the age of 74.<ref name="USU2">{{cite web|url=https://www.creol.ucf.edu/newsevents/NewsDetail.aspx?NewsID=830|title=Professor Boris Zeldovich passes away at age 74|publisher=CREOL, The College of Optics & Photonics|accessdate=27 December 2018|date=18 December 2018|archive-date=27 December 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181227181519/https://www.creol.ucf.edu/newsevents/NewsDetail.aspx?NewsID=830|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="OSAobit">{{cite web|url=https://www.osa.org/en-us/about_osa/newsroom/obituaries/2018/boris_zeldovich_1944-2018/|title=In Memoriam: Boris Zeldovich, 1944–2018|publisher=OSA: The Optical Society|accessdate=26 June 2019}}</ref><ref name="SPIEobit">{{cite web|url=http://www.spie.org/news/0111-boris_zeldovich_obit|title=In Memoriam: Boris Zel'dovich|publisher=SPIE: The International Society for Optics and Photonics|accessdate=26 June 2019|date=11 January 2019}}</ref><ref name="OPNremembering">{{cite magazine|url=https://www.osa-opn.org/home/articles/volume_30/march_2019/departments/remembering_boris_zeldovich/|title=Remembering Boris Zeldovich: 1944–2018|date=1 March 2019|magazine=Optics & Photonics News (OPN)|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230429165316/https://www.optica-opn.org/opn/media/Images/PDF/2019/0319/51_OPN_03_19.pdf|archive-date=2023-04-29|publisher=The Optical Society|access-date=26 June 2019|first1=Nadia|last1=Baranova|first2=Leon|last2=Glebov|first3=Alexander|last3=Kaplan|first4=Nelson|last4=Tabiryan}}</ref>
